description: DB integration: existing workspace allocations read as `workspace` after migration, and the kind-aware constraints reject a seat row with a customer tenant and a workspace row without one.
Unit: capability matrix for `co-managed-seat` across flag, entitlement, product code, participation and both `FORCE_CAPABILITIES` values, with `co-managed` unaffected.
DB integration: the capacity function equals the previous three queries on a pool with workspace-only allocations, and counts seat rows once on a mixed pool.
DB integration: seat reservation happy path and replay by operation id; refused for insufficient capacity, ineligible sponsor and lapse grace.
DB integration, concurrent: with one seat available, a seat reservation and a workspace reservation race and exactly one succeeds.
DB integration: resize refuses a decrease below committed seats; release returns seats once and a replay changes nothing; a purchase reduction below allocated across both kinds is refused.
DB integration: capacity below allocated with only seat allocations starts grace and then read-only on the same deadlines as a workspace pool.
DB integration: arrangement creation is atomic with its allocation, replays to the same arrangement, and is refused for an inactive client and for a client with a live workspace relationship.
DB integration, concurrent: eight invitations against one remaining seat produce one success; an invitation for an email claimed by another tenant's internal user is refused with that reason.
DB integration, concurrent: seat admission running against reservation, purchase intent and hosted reconcile completes without deadlock.

DB integration: accepting an invitation creates an internal user with only the seat role; the role and its permissions exist for that tenant and no other, and the role editor omits them for a tenant not served.
DB integration: with a tenant at its licensed seat limit, seat technicians can still be added up to the allocation, and every licence count site returns the same number as before they existed.

DB integration: revoking a seat deactivates the user and frees the seat; converting a seat technician to an MSP user is refused at the MSP seat limit and succeeds with a free seat; assigning a non-seat role or a team to a seat technician is refused.
DB integration: an empty board scope yields no ticket access and a board marked no-create refuses ticket creation.

Unit, property: seat subject against every resource type and action in the kernel catalog, asserting own-client allow, other-client deny, out-of-scope board deny, unshared project deny and unnamed resource deny, each with its reason.
Contract: adding a resource type to the kernel catalog without classifying it for seat subjects fails; the policy service lists no seat rule as editable.

E2E: a seat technician's menu shows only the operational surface; requesting billing, settings, user administration, dispatch and reports routes answers not found; an API key cannot be created and a REST request is refused.

DB integration: a seat technician and a portal user calling the service catalog and contract-line lookups are refused; an internal user with permission succeeds; a client read by a seat technician contains no billing column.
DB integration: a seat technician's user list, assignee options and mention suggestions contain no user outside the projection and no MSP staff email or phone.
DB integration: after revoking an assignment or removing a board from scope, the technician's next request is denied without a new sign-in.
Query budget: native ticket list, ticket detail, comment write and time-entry paths for a tenant not served run the same statement count as on main.
Unit: audience truth table over audience, reader organization and requester flag, with inconsistent legacy rows resolving private; the SQL form agrees with the TypeScript form on the same rows.
DB integration: a ticket with ten legacy internal notes shows a seat technician none of them, in the conversation, the activity list, attachments and search.
DB integration: MSP staff post shared IT on an arrangement client's ticket and are refused on another client's ticket; a seat technician is refused a private note and a legacy internal note.
DB integration: a reply inherits its thread's audience; a seat technician cannot change audience; an MSP widening without confirmation is refused.
E2E: a seat technician opens the native ticket list, sees only their client's in-scope tickets, and each view's count matches its rows.

E2E: on the native ticket screen a seat technician sees no billing, materials, credentials, bundle, delete or scheduling affordance and no billing profile picker; the network log shows no billing rollup or materials request.

DB integration: a seat technician creates a ticket for their client; a request naming another client or an out-of-scope board is refused; an edit changing the client or moving to an out-of-scope board is refused.

DB integration: assigning a seat technician is accepted on an own-client in-scope ticket and refused on another client's ticket, an out-of-scope board and a task of an unshared project; the technician's picker lists no MSP user.
DB integration: hand to MSP and hand to client IT change responsibility, store a receipt, replay to the original receipt, and fail on a stale revision or an out-of-scope board.
E2E: an MSP technician hands a ticket to client IT from the native screen, the seat technician sees it under Client IT, hands it back, and the MSP sees the chip change.

E2E: on an arrangement client's ticket the MSP composer shows three audiences defaulting to Private and the picker shows a Client IT group; on another client's ticket both are unchanged; the technician's composer shows two audiences.
DB integration: MSP SLA elapsed time does not advance while responsibility is with client IT and resumes after handback; a ticket of a client with no arrangement is unaffected.

DB integration: a bulk handoff over a mixed selection acts on qualifying tickets and reports each failure; the responsibility filter returns the expected rows; a seat technician creating a tag is refused.

E2E: a seat technician opens the time-entry dialog and saves an entry; the network log shows no service catalog, tax or contract request, and the stored entry is operational with no service or contract line.
DB integration: a billing run, invoice preview, unbilled-time list and approval queue for the period do not include seat technician entries; the technician lists, edits and deletes their own.
DB integration: the effort summary hides the MSP total from a seat technician by default, shows it when the arrangement allows, and shows both totals to MSP staff.

DB integration: a seat technician sees only shared projects; the project and task reads contain no budget, billing or rate key; task status, assignment, comment and time writes succeed on a shared project and fail on an unshared one.

DB integration: a seat technician reads own-client assets with inventory fields and no billing profile or purchase cost, another client's asset answers not found, and no remote or script action is reachable; linking an asset to a ticket and creating a ticket from an asset succeed.
DB integration: a seat technician reads client-visible documents and client-audience articles, and is refused an internal-only document, an internal-audience article and any stored credential.
DB integration: handoff with and without a named technician, handoff to the MSP and a shared IT note each notify the expected recipients and no one else.

DB integration: the rendered email to a seat technician for a ticket with private notes contains no private text, a private note produces no technician notification, and a seat technician added as a watcher on an out-of-scope ticket is admitted and receives only the requester-audience client rendering (no MSP link, no shared IT or private content), while on an in-scope ticket they receive their audience's rendering.
Integration with the email emulator: a seat technician's reply to a shared IT notification is stored as shared IT and a reply to a requester notification as requester.

E2E: on a client with no arrangement an administrator chooses Seat, sets seats, scope and a first technician, and the overview shows the arrangement with pool totals reduced; choosing Workspace opens the existing provisioning flow.
E2E with the Stripe emulator: an allocation larger than available capacity leads to a purchase review for the new total and completes with one charge.
E2E: user administration lists a seat technician under their client apart from MSP staff with licence usage unchanged, and the effective access view explains a denial caused by board scope.
Contract: no seat UI file reads the raw release flag, and with the capability off the client tab, overview rows and ticket affordances are absent.

DB integration: ending an arrangement deactivates technicians, releases the allocation once, returns responsibility to the MSP and leaves shared notes readable by MSP staff; a replay changes nothing; reactivating a technician without a live assignment is refused.
DB integration: after grace expires a seat technician's write is refused with the lifecycle error while reads succeed, and an MSP user and a requester on the same ticket are unaffected.

DB integration: client delete, merge and inactivate are refused while an arrangement is live; a contract test finds every arrangement table in the client-owned roster; changing a ticket's client or board clears the technician assignee and returns responsibility to the MSP.
